title: Prosecutor v. Galić — terror against the civilian population
question: Did the campaign of sniping and shelling against the besieged city constitute the crime of terror against the civilian population, as a violation of the laws or customs of war?
facts: Over a period of approximately 23 months, forces under the accused's command conducted sniping and shelling attacks against civilian areas of a besieged city. The attacks struck civilians going about daily activities — queuing for water, attending funerals, crossing intersections. The pattern was sustained rather than isolated, and included attacks with no identifiable military objective in the vicinity. The accused held effective command over the forces conducting the attacks and received regular reports on their activities.
holding: The Trial Chamber, by majority, found the accused guilty under Article 3 of the Statute of acts of violence the primary purpose of which is to spread terror among the civilian population, as set forth in Article 51 of Additional Protocol I. It founded jurisdiction over that crime on Article 51 of Additional Protocol I, which the parties had brought into effect between themselves by an agreement of 22 May 1992. It found that the accused ordered the campaign of attacks and convicted him under Article 7(1) of the Statute only. (Customary criminal liability for the prohibition of terror was later affirmed by the Appeals Chamber, by majority, in 2006; it is not the Trial Chamber's ground.)
key_reasoning: Article 51(2) of Additional Protocol I prohibits acts or threats of violence the primary purpose of which is to spread terror among the civilian population
The prohibition bound the parties through their agreement of 22 May 1992, which brought Article 51 of Additional Protocol I into effect

The attacks were not isolated incidents but a widespread or systematic campaign with no discernible significance in military terms, from which the Majority found the primary purpose of spreading terror
The accused, through his orders and other means of facilitation and encouragement, conducted the campaign, establishing responsibility under Article 7(1)
